title: Global sections on scheme modules is additive and left exact
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ be the abelian category of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The global-sections functor $\Gamma(X,-):\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)\to\operatorname{Ab}$, $\mathcal F\mapsto\mathcal F(X)$, is additive and preserves kernels; hence it is left exact in the sense of [def-sp-left-exact-additive].

source.place: Cohomology of Sheaves, Lemma Tag 01EZ (lemma-before-Leray), proof setup for $\Gamma(Y,-)$

proof.text: Unfold the global-sections functor as toPresheaf X followed by evaluation at the top open. Addition of module-sheaf morphisms is sectionwise by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], so mapping f + g gives the sum of the two section maps by definitional equality. This constructs Functor.Additive directly.

The sectionwise-limit theorem [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-limits-sectionwise] is implemented for schemes by the Mathlib PreservesLimits instance for AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf. Evaluation also preserves limits (CategoryTheory.Limits.evaluationPreservesLimits). Instantiate both preservation classes explicitly, then infer preservation of the parallel-pair diagram (f, 0) by composition. This is the kernel-preservation clause of the statement.

proof_origin.place: Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf preserves limits (Sheaf.lean:78); evaluationPreservesLimits (Basic.lean:405); sectionwise addition gives additivity by rfl
